blocks.title: Le Chatelier's principle
blocks.text: If a system in equilibrium is disturbed, it behaves in such a way as to nullify the effect of that disturbance.

The principle describes what happens to a system when something momentarily takes it away from equilibrium. Henry-Louis Le Chatelier (1850-1936), a French chemist of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, proposed it, a significant achievement in chemistry.

blocks.prompt: State Le Chatelier's principle and use it to predict what an equilibrium mixture does when some of a product is removed.
blocks.explanation: A disturbed equilibrium shifts so as to cancel the disturbance. Removing a product lowers its concentration, so the system makes more of it: the equilibrium shifts towards the products until a new equilibrium is reached.

items: Le Chatelier (1850-1936): a disturbed equilibrium shifts to nullify the disturbance.
